policy: web-security-upstream is strict and opt-in: observed Moli differences are failures, never rewritten expectations. Chrome-only internals are inventoried with explicit reasons instead of reported as passing ports.

entries.notes: Preserve default and disabled controls, preflight/Origin server witnesses, and all three canvas readback entry points. HTTP canvas variants isolate taint behavior from local-file loader availability.
These exercise the independent allow-file-access-from-files switch or an embedder-only allow_universal_access_from_file_urls preference, not disable-web-security. Moli does not expose either setting.
Sandbox allow-scripts, local file document and local image, including the default-mode rejection control.
Cross-origin XHR reads an ORB-protected document MIME type. Existing web-security/orb also tests no-cors Fetch response filtering.

Real cross-origin registration/query; update and unregister run in the child Window Realm, without requiring parent access to a possibly remote frame. The workers are installed through the public API rather than a browser-internal hook.

Port the flag-dependent origin exception, trustworthy localhost positive control, insecure HTTP document rejection, and disallowed-scheme invariant through public APIs. The upstream HTTPS trustworthy-origin branch is represented by loopback HTTP, without adding fake TLS or disabling certificate validation.

Cross-origin getRegistration can find the remote registration in disabled mode, while own getRegistrations remains empty and the remote origin retains its registration. This tests public lookup/storage isolation, not Chromium StorageKey object equality.

Port the OAC response header, originAgentCluster value and cross-origin parent access. The 147 C++ fixture additionally forces same-process origin isolation; our 156 oracle intentionally retains desktop default Site Isolation, and records the resulting parent-access restriction rather than disabling isolation to make access succeed.

Replace testRunner.overridePreference(WebKitWebSecurityEnabled,false) with the startup flag. Mutate the data: SVG child background after an initial screenshot; assert both DOM access and painted before/after pixels. Default mode is a negative control.
Port the exact loopback-to-loopback resource request and verify isSecureContext remains unchanged. This does not claim to test public-to-private network permission enforcement.

These assert RenderFrameHostImpl::BuildClientSecurityState on synthetic secure/insecure public-address-space fixtures. Moli has no ClientSecurityState/LNA permission model or equivalent browser-internal API; loopback success alone would not be an equivalent port.

AllAllowMap enumerates internal secure-context, allow-insecure, IP-address-space and request-context inputs. There is no corresponding Moli LNA policy function; do not substitute a single successful fetch for this matrix.
Keep the observable denial of a chrome-untrusted://resources script. Moli has no WebUI URLDataSource or Mojo bindings; the Chrome-specific implementation and process-kill assertions are not ported.

Port the script-initiated iframe/main-frame/window.open denial through CDP committed URLs. Moli cannot install Chromium WebUI controllers or assert RenderProcessHost/SiteInstance identities; nonexistent privileged URLs do not test WebUI bindings isolation.
Port web-initiated local/privileged destination blocking, including the original window.open path. The C++ process/site-instance and forged-navigation assertions have no Moli equivalent.
Directly forge BeginNavigation Mojo IPC fields and require a renderer bad-message process kill. Neither the IPC nor the process security model exists in Moli; JS cannot construct the tested input.

Uses isolate-origins=http://b.is and an invalid blob navigation to assert renderer process transfers and RenderFrameProxyHost topology. Moli has no site-isolated remote-frame process representation. Upstream itself disables this test on Linux/Windows.

Uses WebUI bindings and browser URLLoaderFactory injection to emulate a compromised renderer and assert process termination. Other inherited cache/crash/network-service tests use the flag only as fixture scaffolding, not as their assertion subject.
Public XHR to a filesystem: URL is still rejected; this covers only the observable unsupported-scheme guard, not forged browser-side URLLoaderFactory requests from a WebUI process.
Port denial of XHR to chrome-extension:. The installed-extension/process-security scenario is unavailable in Moli and the upstream test is disabled for Site Isolation incompatibility.

Related tests disable the WebKit preference rather than the flag. Require installed Chrome extensions, apps/webview guests, privileged blob/filesystem URL factories and extension process locks. Moli does not implement this platform.

Bad-flag infobars, enterprise warning policy, kiosk windows and profile-picker UI; none exists in Moli headless fetch/serve. Instance-specific profile/config behavior is already covered by the Moli CLI web-security tests.

The flag is setup for cross-port DRM license servers, not the subject of these media/decryption tests. Moli has no CDM/license-server playback implementation. Cross-port Fetch/XHR is already tested in web-security.

Disable CORS on the internal loader used to issue OPTIONS so preflights do not recursively preflight themselves. The suite tests PreflightController, not the CLI flag. Existing web-security PUT witnesses assert one OPTIONS in default mode and none in disabled mode.
Android-only bound_network/NetworkHandle internal network-factory behavior; skipped by upstream on desktop and has no Moli desktop equivalent.
Android-only URLRequestContext bound-network propagation; disabled security is fixture configuration, not the tested behavior.
Additional negative XHR controls for browser-owned schemes. These are not presented as ports of Chrome WebUI/extension process internals.
